questions.cardText:
[Cultural Studies] Traditionally, how might Uyghur people indicate that a location is far away?
A. By stretching out the pronunciation of the locative adverb (“It is theeeeeeeeeere!”)
B. By saying the locative adverb louder (“It is THERE!”)
C. By repeating the locative adverb multiple times (“It is there, there, there, there, there!”)
Answer: A.
questions.de: Was entscheidet im Uigurischen, welches Demonstrativpronomen („dieser“ oder „jener“) ein Sprecher wählt?
questions.en: In Uyghur, what decides which demonstrative pronoun ('this' or 'that') a speaker chooses?

timeline.labelEn: Engesæth, Yakup and Dwyer publish a Uyghur grammar describing demonstratives chosen by distance from the speaker
timeline.labelDe: Engesæth, Yakup und Dwyer veröffentlichen eine uigurische Grammatik, die nach Entfernung gewählte Demonstrativa beschreibt

questions.notes: The card claims Uyghur speakers stretch the word 'there' ("theeeere!") to show a place is far away; no source confirms this (Uyghur grammar descriptions only show that vowel length marks stress). The open question asks the verified fact behind the card's theme: Uyghur demonstratives (bu 'this', u 'that', shu, and the intensified mawu/awu) are chosen by the referent's distance from the speaker.

questions.cardText:
[Botany] Which one of the following is botanically a berry?
A. Tomato
B. Raspberry
C. Cherry
Answer: A. Botanically, a berry is a fleshy fruit produced from a single ovary that usually contains several seeds. As such, raspberries, blackberries, and strawberries are not true berries.
questions.de: Welche Frucht aus der Familie der Nachtschattengewächse, die der Oberste Gerichtshof der USA 1893 zum „Gemüse“ erklärte, ist botanisch eine Beere?
questions.en: Which nightshade-family fruit, ruled a 'vegetable' by the US Supreme Court in 1893, is botanically a berry?

timeline.labelEn: In Nix v. Hedden the US Supreme Court rules tomatoes are vegetables, not fruit, for tariff purposes
timeline.labelDe: Im Fall Nix v. Hedden erklärt der Oberste Gerichtshof der USA Tomaten für Zollzwecke zu Gemüse, nicht zu Obst

questions.notes: Tomatoes are listed as true berries (Solanaceae) in Wikipedia's Berry (botany); raspberries are aggregate fruits and cherries drupes. Clue chosen to single out the tomato among the many true berries (grapes, bananas, eggplants …); date from the Nix v. Hedden article.
